note: One golf swing filmed on a phone: bone transforms, muscle paths and 3D joints. Skeleton time t is the master clock (phases + findings use t; video seeks to t+offset). Hands/wrists use locked-wrist OpenSim IK (no SOMA palm retarget).

findings.title: Shoulders turn past the hips
findings.headline: Your shoulders out-turn your hips at the top
findings.plain: At the top the shoulders have turned about 39° past the hips. That stretch is the one to keep — the downswing gets its speed from letting it unwind, hips first.
findings.why: The gap between shoulders and hips stretches the trunk at the top. Speed comes from letting that stretch unwind, hips first — not from throwing the arms.
findings.cue: Let the hips stop turning before the shoulders do. Keep the trail knee flexed so the hips stay quiet.
findings.drill: Pause at the top for a count of two, then start down with the lead hip, not the arms. Eight reps.
findings.check: Shoulders-past-hips at the top stays near 39°, with the hips quiet before the shoulders unwind.

metric.caption: shoulders past hips at the top

findings.title: Lead arm bends
findings.headline: Your front arm collapses at the top
findings.plain: At the top of the backswing your front arm bends about 44° (it was nearly straight at address). That shortens the swing arc, so the club has less room to build speed.
findings.why: A bent lead arm narrows the swing radius, so the clubhead has less time to build speed.
findings.cue: At the top, keep the front arm long — stretch it away from your head, not chicken-winged in.
findings.drill: Pump drill. Pause at the top with the lead arm extended, pump down halfway twice, then swing through. Eight reps.
findings.check: Lead elbow flex at the top stays under 30° instead of 44°.

findings.title: Lead arm stays bent
findings.headline: The front arm never fully recovers after impact
findings.plain: Through the finish the front arm is still bent around 65–70°. The arc that collapsed at the top never opens back up.
findings.why: If the lead arm stays collapsed after impact, you lose width through the ball and the club exits high and left of the target line.
findings.cue: After impact, feel the front arm extend toward the target — long and high into the finish.
findings.drill: Finish-hold. Hit half-swings and freeze for two counts with both arms long past the ball. Ten reps.
findings.check: Front-arm bend after impact drops below 40° instead of holding near 70°.
